long_biography.plain_text:
Bruce Milne emerged in Washington's early software industry as chief executive of Accountants Microsystems and the first chairman of the organization that later became the Washington Technology Industry Association. He built AMI into a major vertical-market software company, then sold the business. Research at Harvard Business School and the resulting book Power Planning helped shape his approach to company structure and growth.

Milne founded Corum in 1985 to mentor software companies through a strategic-audit process. Clients repeatedly needed capital, international partners and transaction advice, leading the firm to develop a specialist technology M&A model around research, buyer knowledge and experienced former executives. He remains Corum's founder and chief executive, combining his earlier operator experience with long-term advisory work for privately held technology businesses.
